title: Talent pipeline sprint + assimilate kit
summary: A compact playbook for running a two-week hiring sprint focused on fast, evidence-driven decisions plus a pragmatic first-14-day assimilation checklist for new ICs and managers.
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a lightweight kit to run a 14-day talent pipeline sprint (screen -> take-home -> onsites or pairing) with timeboxed decision gates and an assimilation checklist for day0->14. Goal: reduce time-to-offer without sacrificing evidence quality; make new hires ship-ready earlier via micro-assignments and mentor rotations.

When to use:
- Emergency backfill or high-priority role (customer-impacting, revenue-critical)
- Small candidate pools where speed wins
- Hiring windows tied to product sprints

Core principles:
1) Timebox, don’t shortcut evidence: every stage has a max time and a minimum deliverable.
2) Role-focused probes: design exercises that reflect day-30 work (not trivia).
3) Distributed evidence: require at least two stakeholders (peer + hiring manager) to sign off.
4) Early assimilation: assign a micro-project/week-1 deliverable before offer acceptance where possible (paid stipend for externals).

Sprint flow (14 days) - high level:
Day 0-2: slate + rapid phone screen (30 min)
Day 2-5: take-home or paid pairing (48-72h turnaround)
Day 5-9: onsite loop or two deep pairing sessions (4-6h total)
Day 10: decision gate (offer / reject / follow-up)
Day 11-14: offer acceptance + pre-boarding tasks + buddy calendar confirmed

Decision gates and artifacts (min viable evidence):
- Phone screen: checklist pass/fail (role motivation, basics, communication).
- Take-home/pairing: artifact = repo/zip + short readme or pairing notes. Must show approach + tradeoffs.
- Onsite/pairing: scored rubric (see rubric section). At least one scenario must be system-design or debugging a production bug relevant to role.
- Hiring manager conclave: documented pros/cons and a clear ask (level, comp band).

Scorecard (numeric, simple):
- Technical competency (0-5)
- Product sense / prioritization (0-5)
- Collaboration / communication (0-5)
- Ownership / delivery evidence (0-5)
- Role fit signals (0-5)
Recommendation: require average >=3.5 and no dimension below 2 unless exceptions explicated.

Interview rubric (example question families) - for SWE/Platforms:
- Debugging: give a small reproducer; ask for root-cause, fix, tests, and deploy plan.
- System capacity: describe a latency outage and tradeoffs for mitigations.
- Runtime knowledge: talk through KV cache behavior and expected failure modes.
- Collaboration: any cross-team incident postmortem you influenced? what was your role?
Scoring notes: prefer concrete examples, measurable impact, and tradeoff articulation.

Onboarding / Assimilation checklist (Day 0 -> Day 14)
Pre-Day0 (offer accepted):
- HR: benefits packet + start paperwork (due D-3)
- IT: laptop + keycard order, access to internal docs list
- Manager: shared 14-day plan and first impactful micro-task
- Buddy: intro email and calendar invites for first week

Day 0 (first day):
- 1:1 with manager (30m): expectations, success metrics for 14d, immediate blockers
- Buddy intro (60m): walkthrough of codebase top-3 paths, product context, where devs spend 80% of time
- Quick wins list: 3 labeled issues of increasing complexity (small, medium, medium+)
- System access: verify repo, CI, internal slack channels, deployment perms

Days 1-3:
- Micro-assignment 1 (small): fix a bug or add a test; PR + review within 48h
- Pairing session with peer (90m): set up local env and run end-to-end scenario
- Doc sprint: update or add a README for the touched component (owner: new hire)

Days 4-7:
- Micro-assignment 2 (medium): implement a small feature or performance tweak; deliverables: PR + perf notes
- Product sync (30m): join product standup and present the micro-assignment outcomes
- Mentor rotation: 1:1 with 2 other engineers for 30m each to broaden context

Days 8-14:
- Micro-assignment 3 (integrative): work on a cross-cutting fix/feature; coordinate with SRE or infra owner
- 14-day readout: 20m demo + 10m discussion on learning, blockers, and 30-day roadmap
- Probability check: manager records go/no-go signals for autonomy and escalation timeline

Manager & Buddy playbook (quick bullets):
- Manager: set measurable 14d outcomes; give continuous feedback; unblock access requests same-day
- Buddy: be available for low-friction pairing (first two weeks), ensure 3 contextual docs exist after week 1
- Hiring manager to decide on skills remediation plan if average rubric <4 by day 14

Probation readout format (template):
- One-paragraph summary of contributions
- Top 3 strengths observed
- Top 3 risks / skill gaps and remediation plan
- Recommendation and target autonomy date

Signals to escalate (red flags):
- Repeated inability to run local stack after 3 pairing sessions
- Poor cross-team communication observed in demos or PR comments
- Delivery gaps on committed micro-assignments without good rationale

Legal / comp notes (ops):
- For expedited paid pairing tasks: cap stipend at $500 and track through People Ops vendor pool
- Ensure offer letters include probation expectations when applicable and compensation band

Templates (copy-paste friendly snippets):
- Manager intro email to new hire: "Welcome — quick plan for first two weeks + buddy details + immediate ask (first micro-task)"
- Buddy kickoff message: short checklist to run the new hire through local setup and 2 short pair sessions
- 14-day readout prompt: "Please prepare a 10-minute demo covering what you built, decisions you made, and next steps."

Open questions / next improvements (notes for People Ops team):
- Pilots: trial paid pairing for contractor hires vs salaried candidates, measure acceptance velocity
- Automations: pre-populate 14-day calendar invites via HR system integration
- Metrics: time-to-offer, offer-acceptance rate, % of hires with positive 14-day readout

Attachments / quick references (links):
- Standard offer template: CONFLUENCE-4567
- Paid-pairing vendor list: JIRA-OPS-1982
- Hiring dashboard: internal analytics report (weekly)

Notes to self: iterate micro-assignments library for infra, console, and SRE roles. Run a 2-role pilot this quarter with engineering leadership and report outcomes in People Ops weekly.
notes: This is intentionally compact and action-oriented. Keep the artifacts lean and the gates strict. Use human judgment for exceptions and record rationale in linked_artifacts.
